motivation: According to the Lotka-Volterra equations, prey reproduction follows exponential growth in the absence of predation. The prey birth rate is proportional to the current prey population: dR/dt (births) = αR, where R is prey population and α is the birth rate coefficient. More prey means more breeding individuals, directly causing higher birth rates.

This is a fundamental stock-flow relationship. Births are an inflow to the prey population stock. An increase in the birth rate directly causes an increase in the prey population over time: R(t+dt) = R(t) + births*dt.

In the Lotka-Volterra model, prey deaths occur through predator-prey encounters. The death rate is proportional to prey population: deaths = βRP, where β is the predation rate coefficient, R is prey, and P is predators. More prey means more potential encounters with predators, causing higher death rates.
The Lotka-Volterra predation term βRP shows that prey death rate increases with predator population. More predators means more hunting, more encounters with prey, and thus higher prey mortality.

Deaths are an outflow from the prey population stock. An increase in death rate directly causes a decrease in prey population: R(t+dt) = R(t) - deaths*dt. This is a fundamental conservation principle.

Predator reproduction depends on food availability. In Lotka-Volterra, predator births = δRP, where δ is the conversion efficiency of prey to predator offspring. More prey means more food, enabling higher predator reproduction rates.

Predator births require existing predators to reproduce. The birth rate scales with predator population: births = δRP. More predators means more breeding individuals, causing higher total birth rates (given sufficient prey).
Births are an inflow to the predator population stock. An increase in birth rate directly causes an increase in predator population: P(t+dt) = P(t) + births*dt.

In the Lotka-Volterra model, predator deaths occur at a rate proportional to population: deaths = γP, where γ is the natural death rate. More predators means more individuals that can die, causing higher total death rates.
Deaths are an outflow from the predator population stock. An increase in death rate directly causes a decrease in predator population: P(t+dt) = P(t) - deaths*dt.
